## Public-primary reduction checked after independent reconstruction
The actual final Bacher--de la Harpe--Nagnibeda, BSMF125(2)(1997)167-198, DOI10.24033/bsmf.2303, Proposition8 p179 and proof pp190-191, states N^1(G) is isometric to Lambda^1(G*) for a sphere planar dual. This is an earlier printed lattice theorem, not an earlier printed Conjecture4.11 solution.
Their Section1 pp168-169 allows finite loops and multiple edges. Choosing one orientation identifies their antisymmetric cochains with Z^E: the factor1/2 in their two-orientation dot product makes the chosen-coordinate metric exactly the ordinary dot product. Their d is B^t and d* is B. Since <z,BB^t z>=||B^t z||^2, ker(dd*)=ker(d*), so Lambda^1(H)=ker B_H integrally. Their N^1(G)=Z^E intersect im_R B^t equals im_Z B^t: if z=B^t f is integer, subtract f(r) from every potential; path sums show every resulting potential integer. This supplies the saturation bridge rather than assuming it. The paper also prints this equality and the root-omitted Z-basis on p182, and the Gram entries on p183 (loops contribute zero).
Proposition8's proof sends oriented circuits to oriented dual bonds, preserves signed edge inner products and invokes integral bases. Lemma2 pp181-182 actually proves integral fundamental-cycle/fundamental-bond bases by eliminating respectively nontree/tree coefficients: a residual tree circulation is zero by deleting leaves; a gradient vanishing on a spanning tree is constant and hence zero. The dual circuit/bond bridge follows from the Jordan curve theorem: the two complementary sides give connected dual regions (paths within either open disk can be made transverse to finitely many edges); the crossed edges are exactly the cut, and deleting any proper subset leaves a crossing, so the cut is a bond. Conversely a minimal separating dual edge cut has one primal boundary circuit, since a second circuit would make it nonminimal. Loops and two-edge circuits are included. Alternatively the explicit signed facial generation above supplies the same integral equality without a Voronoi or Whitney theorem. No determinant-group-only assertion is substituted for lattice isometry.
Apply Proposition8 separately to G1 and G2. Both are finite connected planar graphs, a permitted subclass of the paper's multigraphs. Their specified sphere duals H1,H2 have all loop/multiplicity data retained. The given multigraph isomorphism acts on cochains by a signed permutation, preserving both the metric and incidence kernel. Thus N^1(G1) is isometric to Lambda^1(H1), then Lambda^1(H2), then N^1(G2). Root-omitted bases have rank n_i-1; isometry gives equal n_i, also Euler gives the same equality. Their Grams are exactly the source reduced Laplacians, so the A and S_i argument already proved gives a full integer unimodular U. For n=1 the lattice is zero and the full matrix is [0]; for trees the dual loop flows are Z^E. Therefore every hypothesis and the full singular conclusion of cached Conjecture4.11 are covered. The lift from this earlier lattice theorem to the conjecture is the present explicit reduction; it is not claimed verbatim in the 1997 paper. This establishes a complete routine-application objection, independent of any unread final2026 correction.
